Flock flying very low (maybe 30 ft) overhead going S right over the MB05 pullout where we parked. Heard very well calling “kip-kip-kip,” then looked up to see a flock of stocky birds with short tails in bouncing flight. Seemed slightly larger and more heavyset than Purple Finches, which we saw throughout the morning. Attempted audio recording, but they were gone into the Stevens Creek drainage. This seems to be a good spot for them in the past, even in years without massive montane irruptions.

Resident birds. Rare in the county but now established here and breeding. This small flock was perched in a willow tree here  37.247840416807094, -121.87044567976321 and was making frequent trips down into the reeds and grasses to gather food, offering great views. 5 of the birds were adults but interestingly there were 3 juvenile birds hidden in the willow tree giving begging calls and fluttering their wings. They were pretty young (some yellow still showing on their gapes and unscaled buffy breasts) which seems weird for this late in the season (possibly a second or third brood?). The birds were flying down into the grass and bringing seeds back to their young. ID: Small finch-like birds; reddish brown overall with large conical black bills and black scaling on the breast. Juveniles were similar to adults but lacked the patterning on the underside and still had some fluff on their heads. Photos + audio to follow.

Spotted by Liam at about 2:05pm.  It appeared over the cypresses to the north east, fairly high, and making a beeline to the North or NNE toward Marin.   It took me a few precious seconds to get on it - but when I did, it was obviously a pale falcon with long, tapered wings, and a pale face and underwing pattern, with some streaking on the neck and breast.   Caitlin called Prairie Falcon, and I called "dark armpits" characteristic to me of a juvie prairie.  Then we got a clearer view of the tail, which was sandy, pale colored like the rest of the body (eliminating MIKI in my mind).   Liam and Nancy got some diagnostic photos.  Awesome bird.

Flight call flyover from a finch-sized bird. Call #3 UT for Cassin's Finch in Sibley app is a direct match. Brief view going away showed light, or pale underparts, so likely am immature/female type.

Very familiar with all flight calls of regularly occurring species at this location. My very first thought after hearing the call was Cassin's Finch, and the first call I played immediately after the flyover (so the call was fresh on my mind) on the Sibley app was a match (call #3). 

It was larger than pine siskin and goldfinches. No sparrow, horned lark, crossbill  or longspur would be match for the call. I am familiar with all House and Purple Finch flight calls and can easily rule them out. This species seems to be irruptive this year, so it may not be very unusual to find them about right now.

Gorgeous vagrant seen by many the past few days. Bright rufous tail, Dark brown streaked throat, pale yellow breast, striped head with thick dark eye stripe. Giant bill, feasting on fat red spiders with white-dotted backs.
